title: Policy-led canary orchestrator with deterministic shadow probes and abort predicates
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a policy-driven canary orchestration capability that supports deterministic shadow probing, multi-step traffic schedules, and configurable abort predicates. The goal is a declarative config surface that lets teams express: staged traffic splits, probe profiles (latency, semantic drift, regression tests), quorum rules for approval, and automated rollback triggers tied to telemetry. This ticket implements runtime admission/eviction hooks, a compact DSL for canary manifests, and an authoring UI surface in Console (follow-up PR).
acceptance_criteria: Runtime accepts a new canary manifest and executes a 4-step staged rollout with specified durations and weight splits
Shadow probes can be enabled per-step to mirror 100% of specified subset traffic to the new variant without affecting production responses
Abort predicates (error rate, P50 latency, semantic-similarity delta) fire within configured evaluation windows and trigger a deterministic rollback action
Telemetry events emitted for each step: step_started, shadow_probe_result, metric_evaluation, abort_decision, step_completed
Integration tests cover simulated traffic patterns: normal, gradual degradation, and spike failures — resulting in expected commit, pause, or rollback behaviors
design_notes: Declarative manifest: minimal YAML surface with steps[], predicates[], probe_profiles[] — aim to keep runtime evaluation simple and side-effect free
Deterministic evaluation: use fixed windowing (e.g., 60s) and quorum rules to avoid flaky aborts due to sampling variance
Shadow probing semantics: mirror requests and collect responses into an isolated evaluation pipeline; do not forward mirrored responses to callers
Rollback granularity: support immediate full rollback or step-back-to-previous-step using explicit policy; default is immediate full rollback for high-severity predicates
Performance: runtime kernel must evaluate predicates in <5ms per decision path to avoid adding latency to admission path
Security: mirrored payloads must respect PII redaction and KMS-based access for evaluation artifacts
config_example:
canary:
  id: user-model-v2-intro
  description: Small staged rollout for user-model v2 with semantic drift checks
  steps:
    - name: step-1-smoke
      weight: 0.01
      duration_seconds: 300
      probes: [smoke, latency]
    - name: step-2-shadow
      weight: 0.05
      duration_seconds: 1800
      probes: [semantic-drift, latency]
      shadow: true
    - name: step-3-cohort
      weight: 0.2
      duration_seconds: 3600
      probes: [semantic-drift, business-eval]
    - name: step-4-rollout
      weight: 1.0
      duration_seconds: 0
  predicates:
    - id: high_error_rate
      metric: error_rate
      threshold: 0.02
      window_seconds: 120
      severity: high
      action: rollback
    - id: p50_latency_regress
      metric: p50_latency_ms
      threshold: 250
      window_seconds: 300
      severity: medium
      action: pause
    - id: semantic_drift
      metric: embedding_similarity_delta
      threshold: 0.08
      window_seconds: 900
      severity: high
      action: rollback
  probe_profiles:
    - id: smoke
      sample_rate: 0.5
      quick_checks: [status_code, latency]
    - id: semantic-drift
      sample_rate: 1.0
      evaluator: comparator-service/v1
testing_plan: Unit tests for predicate evaluation logic (edge thresholds, NaNs, empty windows)
Integration tests in local cluster: run fixture traffic generator with controlled regressions to assert expected abort actions
Chaos tests: inject transient latency spikes and verify pause behavior vs. full rollback for sustained errors
End-to-end test: create manifest via API, run rollout, and assert Console shows correct step timeline and emitted telemetry
rollout_plan: Phase A (engine): implement manifest parser, evaluation loop, and action executor behind feature flag
Phase B (integration): wire shadow pipeline and probe collectors; add telemetry schema and metrics
Phase C (pilot): enable feature for 3 internal teams with canaries limited to non-critical models
Phase D (GA): expose authoring surface in Console, document patterns and recommended predicates
telemetry: Emit structured events to observability: canary.manifest.created, canary.step.started, canary.probe.result, canary.predicate.evaluation, canary.action.triggered
Expose per-canary time-series: step_weight, errors, p50/p95 latency, semantic_similarity
Alerting: default SLO-bound alerts when any predicate of severity=high fires; integrate with PagerDuty escalation policy
